data.title: Bankrupt Dish Wireless reaches $525M settlement with American Tower - report
data.description:
EchoStar (ECHO) subsidiary Dish Wireless has reached a $525M settlement with American Tower (AMT) and is in talks with other tower owners who say they're owed billions of dollars after its failed attempt to build a 5G network, according to a media report on Wednesday.

Dish is in the process of hammering out similar deals with other large creditors, including Charter Communications (CHTR),  which provided infrastructure and services for its 5G network, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing a court hearing.

Last year, EchoStar switched strategy and started selling spectrum licenses and winding down the 5G network operations after the Federal Communications Commission pressured Dish for taking too long to build the network.

The settlement funds are being paid from a $2.4B creditor trust established by the FCC using proceeds from AT&T's purchase of EchoStar's spectrum licenses. The settlement with American Tower will require FCC approval, the WSJ said.

Dish Wireless, the EchoStar unit that was building the 5G network, filed for Chapter 11 in June along with Dish DBS, another EchoStar subsidiary, so they could restructure their balance sheets.

data.title: Stocks to watch on Wednesday after hours: PANW, SNEX, MKL, YELP
data.description:
Wall Street's major averages finished mixed on Wednesday after Nvidia reported better-than-expected Q3 results amid the recent CEO scandal. The Nasdaq ended higher even as Nvidia closed lower.

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) finished -0.2%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) ended +0.4, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) finished -1.1%.

Now, here are a few stocks to watch during extended trading hours:

  • Palo Alto Networks (PANW) surged 8% after releasing its first-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results, extending the stock's 9.9% surge logged in the regular trading session. The cybersecurity stalwart turned in adjusted earnings per share of $1.05 versus the $0.97 consensus estimate.
  • StoneX Group (SNEX) stock slid 2.9% as the company's fiscal Q4 earnings failed to meet Wall Street expectations. While operating revenue grew from a year ago but fell from fiscal Q3, its expenses rose both from the prior quarter and a year ago.
  • Markel Group (MKL) said that its board approved a $2.5B increase to its existing share repurchase authorization. Shares edged up 0.5%.
  • Yelp (YELP) disclosed a workforce reduction expected to affect nearly 5% of its full-time employees.

data.title: Borr Drilling reports 9M results
data.description: • Borr Drilling press release (BORR): Total operating revenues decreased by $19.0 million to $742.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $761.4 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease in total operating revenues is due to a decrease in dayrate revenue of $67.7 million, partially offset by an increase in bareboat charter revenue of $41.3 million and management contract revenue of $7.4 million.

data.title: Harmony Gold outlines mine safety actions after two fatalities this week
data.description:
Harmony Gold (HMY) fell 7.3% on Wednesday after saying it is taking steps to improve safety at its operations following two fatalities at its South African mines this week.

Precious metals mining stocks fell across the board Wednesday as gold and silver prices plunged to their lowest levels in nearly 14 months.

Harmony (HMY) said an employee, who had reported having been exposed to chemical fumes during acid treatment activities at the Mine Waste Solutions plant in Stilfontein during an incident on November 16, died in the hospital on November 17.

The incident occurred after an employee was killed while conducting tramming activities in the Carbon Leader Reef development section of the Mponeng mine in Gauteng on November 14.

In response, Harmony (HMY) said it is sharing and applying the findings of both investigations across every operation; improving critical control verification to prevent loss of life at all workplaces; and strengthening ownership and accountability, assurance, hazard identification and workplace examinations throughout the group.

"Zero harm demands unwavering attention and accountability from every leader in Harmony," CEO Beyers Nel said.

data.title: Mitek appoints Laura Apel as chief marketing officer
data.description:
• Mitek Systems (MITK) announced on Wednesday the appointment of Laura Apel as chief marketing officer, effective November 16, 2026.
  • Apel will lead Mitek's global marketing organization, overseeing brand, demand generation, product marketing, and communications, the company added.
  • Most recently, she led global marketing for Vonage's API business unit, an Ericsson company, where she focused on positioning a multi-product portfolio, driving demand and connecting marketing with commercial objectives. 
  • Press Release

data.title: MEDIROM files overdue annual report, appeals Nasdaq delisting notice
data.description:
• MEDIROM Healthcare Technologies (MRM) announced on Wednesday that it filed its overdue fiscal 2025 annual report with the SEC and appealed Nasdaq's delisting decision.

  • The company requested a hearing, which automatically stays trading suspension for 15 days. It also requested an extended stay pending the hearing.

  • The company said the filing addresses its reporting deficiency but does not resolve a separate minimum bid-price requirement, for which Nasdaq granted an extension until April 5, 2027.

data.title: Innoviz launches 1-for-20 reverse stock split to regain Nasdaq compliance
data.description:
• Innoviz Technologies (INVZ) said on Wednesday that it launched a 1-for-20 reverse stock split of its common shares to regain compliance with the Nasdaq's minimum bid price requirement.
  • The split will result in a proportionate reduction of its authorized share capital from 500M to 25M ordinary shares.
  • The reverse share split is expected to become effective on December 4, 2026, and the shares are expected to begin trading on a split-adjusted basis on the Nasdaq at market open on December 7, 2026.
  • Press Release

data.title: Woodward's shares slip as growth outlook slows
data.description:
Woodward (WWD) shares fell 1.3% in extended trading Wednesday after the aerospace and industrial equipment supplier beat quarterly earnings estimates but forecast slower sales growth and lower industrial margins for fiscal 2027.

Before Wednesday’s close, the shares had risen 5.5%, compared with a 7.3% gain for the S&P 500 stock index.

Net income rose to $165.6 million, or $2.74 a share, from $137.6 million, or $2.23 a share, a year earlier. 

Adjusted earnings increased to $2.83 a share from $2.09, beating the Wall Street consensus estimate of $2.52.

Revenue for the fiscal fourth quarter ended Sept. 30 increased 16.6% to $1.16 billion from $995.3 million. That narrowly topped analysts’ estimate of $1.14 billion by about $20 million.

The results show continued strength in aircraft production, repair demand and industrial equipment sales. But the outlook gives investors reasons for caution: sales growth is expected to slow, manufacturing investment is limiting cash generation and industrial margins are projected to decline. Those pressures could help explain the shares’ retreat despite the quarterly earnings beat.

Slower growth and industrial margin pressure ahead

Woodward (WWD) forecast fiscal 2027 sales growth of 6% to 10%, following a 22% increase in fiscal 2026. Adjusted earnings are projected at $10.20 to $10.70 a share, compared with $9.78 in fiscal 2026.

Management said higher investment in manufacturing capabilities and capacity would moderate margin expansion as it prepares to increase production.

The industrial business faces a tougher outlook. Its sales are expected to grow 1% to 5%, while its earnings margin is projected to fall to between 18.2% and 18.7% from 19.6% in fiscal 2026.

The guidance includes a $110 million sales comparison headwind from winding down the China on-highway business. No sales from that business are expected in fiscal 2027.

Aerospace sales are forecast to rise 8% to 13%, with a segment margin of 23.8% to 24.3%, up from 23.6% in fiscal 2026.

Strong aerospace demand supports quarterly results

“In Aerospace, higher aircraft production rates and continued strong inputs to repair centers drove double-digit growth in Commercial OEM and Services,” Chief Executive Chip Blankenship said in the earnings announcement.

Fourth-quarter aerospace sales rose 18% to $781 million. Sales to commercial aircraft manufacturers increased 26%, while commercial services revenue grew 25%.

Aerospace earnings increased 17% to $190 million, but its margin edged down to 24.3% from 24.4%. Higher pricing and sales volumes helped earnings, while inflation and manufacturing investment partly offset those gains. Defense services revenue fell 12%.

Woodward (WWD) makes energy control systems and components, including consumable parts for CFM LEAP, GEnx and CF34 aircraft engines. Its industrial products include high-speed fuel injection systems used in power generation, marine transportation and oil and gas applications.

Industrial quarterly sales increased 14% to $380 million. Segment earnings jumped 61% to $79 million, and its margin expanded to 20.7% from 14.6%, helped by higher volumes and pricing.

Spending reduces free cash flow as debt rises

Fiscal 2026 revenue reached a record $4.36 billion, while adjusted earnings rose 42% to $9.78 a share.

Operating cash flow increased 37% to $646 million, but capital spending climbed to $319 million from $131 million. That pushed annual free cash flow down 4% to $327 million. Fourth-quarter free cash flow fell 28% to $131 million.

Total debt more than doubled to $1.42 billion from $702 million. The company also reported $711 million in share repurchases during the fiscal year.

The fiscal 2027 outlook calls for some improvement in cash generation, with free cash flow of $400 million to $450 million and capital spending of about $290 million.

data.title: A 15% S&P 500 pullback 'hardly unusual' as investors underprice macro risks – Wells Fargo Investment Institute
data.description:
Investors may be too complacent about accumulating macro risks that could soon collide, according to Jennifer Timmerman, global macro analyst at Wells Fargo Investment Institute.

The 12-month CPI rate accelerated to an estimated 4.0% in October—nearly double the Federal Reserve's 2% target—yet markets have largely shrugged off the warning signs.

"Risks that seem manageable in isolation can become more meaningful when they begin to reinforce one another," Timmerman said.

Interest-rate risk may also be underpriced, the analyst warned, noting that the Fed likely has more work to do with inflation still well above its target.

A higher policy rate would quickly filter through to household budgets via steeper borrowing costs on credit cards and auto loans, while corporate financing expenses climb as well, according to Timmerman.

"Combined with higher labor and input costs, that could make profitable growth more difficult for companies and attractive returns harder for investors to earn," she said.

Equity markets continue to price in lofty expectations for the artificial-intelligence investment boom, while oil and financial markets assume a resolution to Middle East tensions that remains elusive, Timmerman observed.

With the S&P 500 (SP500) trading at a full valuation relative to its historical average and roughly 18 months removed from its last correction, the strategist believes a 10%-15% pullback "would hardly be unusual."

Still, she remains constructive on the economic expansion and equity bull market and said a correction would not necessarily signal the end of either.

Rather than treating every decline as a buying opportunity, Timmerman recommends adding equity exposure through monthly or quarterly dollar-cost averaging with disciplined patience and selectivity.

"Keeping sight of the forest means recognizing the risks without losing sight of the opportunities that volatility may create," she said.

data.title: Markel Group boosts share repurchase authorization by $2.5B
data.description:
• Markel Group (MKL) announced on Wednesday that its board approved a $2.5B increase to its existing share repurchase authorization.

  • The company may repurchase shares through open-market or privately negotiated transactions.

  • The authorization has no expiration date, and the timing and amount of repurchases will depend on market conditions and capital needs.
